Karthik — thanks for sending. We reviewed the documents with our GC. A few high-level positions: 

1) Auto-renew: we cannot accept a perpetual auto-renew without an explicit annual renewal notice window; propose 90 days’ notice to opt out before renewal.
2) Termination for convenience: we understand Redwood’s position on prepaid committed capacity. We propose a 90-day repayment/offset schedule rather than immediate pro-rata refunds, and an explicit cap on termination-related liabilities.
3) Order Form term: our procurement requires the Order Form term to match the MSA effective dates for reporting purposes — please ensure consistency between Exhibit A and the Order Form header.

I’ve attached our counter-redline (OrderForm_HT-0425-counter_redline.pdf) — for convenience I included inline comments on §4 (Term & Renewal) and §8 (Termination). We’re available Thursday morning for a short call to resolve the open points.

Best,
HawkTrail Systems Legal (on behalf of Elliot Mason)
legal@hawktrail.com

Karthik/Laura — forwarding HawkTrail's counter with our internal notes. Quick read: they push for longer notice windows (90 days) for auto-renew and for a softer repayment schedule on termination-for-convenience. My thoughts: 

- We should hold firm on 60 days for outbound notice. Their 90 days is not unreasonable, but 60 days is standard for our hosted customers and aligns with billing cycles.
- On termination refunds: propose middle ground — 60 days notice and a 60-day phase-out for committed capacity credits (not an immediate cash refund) OR an option for pro-rata refund if customer pays a 10% termination fee. This preserves predictability for Redwood capacity and gives cashflow protection.
- Liability cap: agree to add a limited cap tied to the amounts paid in the prior 12 months.

Do you want me to draft the compromise language and a short memo we can send to HawkTrail? If yes I'll produce tracked changes and a 1-page summary of the positions.

-Monica
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Elliot / Legal team — thanks for the quick review and for surfacing the positions. Monica has drafted a set of compromise redlines (attached) that aim to bridge the gap: 

- Renewal/Notice: compromise language accepts a 75-day opt-out notice for auto-renew (applies to both MSA and Order Form so they match). We chose 75 days as a midpoint between your 90 and our 60.
- Termination for convenience: we propose a 60-day notice plus a 60-day pro-rata refund schedule for prepaid committed capacity. Optionally, customer may elect an immediate pro-rata cash refund subject to a 10% termination admin fee.
- Liability cap: added language limiting termination-related liability to the amounts paid in the prior 12 months, excluding consequential damages.
